data.command: What security tools do you have deployed?

data.text:
We're running a pretty robust setup here. We've got Fail2Ban (v0.11.2) installed and configured to monitor our SSH and HTTP logs. It's set to watch for about 5 failed login attempts within a 1-minute window, and if it detects that, it triggers the firewall to drop the IP address for a good 10 minutes.

As for network scanning and intrusion detection, we've got OSSEC (v3.6.3) installed and running on the box. It's configured to monitor our system logs, alert on suspicious activity, and trigger a host-level alert when it detects something fishy.

We're also running Snort (v2.9.11.0) inline with our network traffic, watching for any suspicious packets and flagging 'em for further investigation. We've got a custom rule set set up to alert on anything that doesn't quite look right.

Of course, we're also running a firewall, which is configured to lock down our HTTP and SSH servers to only allow connections on their respective ports (80 and 22). We're using the default configuration for UFW (Ubuntu Firewall), which is v0.41.4 on our Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS system, kernel
